questions.text: Statements: All pens are pencils. Some pencils are erasers. No eraser is a marker. Conclusions: I. Some pens are erasers. II. No pen is a marker. III. Some pencils are not markers.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Draw Venn: All pens ⊂ pencils. Some pencils ∩ erasers ≠ ∅. Erasers ∩ markers = ∅. Since some pencils are erasers and no eraser is marker, those pencils are not markers ⇒ Some pencils are not markers (III). I and II are not forced. Full: From 'All pens are pencils' and 'Some pencils are erasers', pens may or may not be erasers. 'No eraser is marker' only removes markers from erasers, not from all pencils. Thus only conclusion III logically follows.

questions.text: Choose the word which is most nearly opposite in meaning to the word 'EPHEMERAL'.
questions.solution: The word 'ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time. Options B, C, and D are synonyms (temporary, fleeting, transient). By eliminating the three synonyms, the only antonym left is 'Permanent'. Hence, option A is correct.

questions.text: Choose the phrasal verb that best fits the blank to make the sentence contextually and grammatically correct. The management decided to ______ the outdated policy after widespread protests from the staff.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Context clue 'outdated policy' + 'protests' implies abolition/removal. Eliminate meanings: 'Do up' = renovate/fasten; 'Do without' = manage in absence; 'Do over' = repeat. Only 'Do away with' means abolish. Step-by-step: 1) Analyze context: Management reacting to protests against an old policy -> likely scrapping it. 2) Test Option A: 'Do up the policy' (renovate? incorrect collocation). 3) Test Option B: 'Do away with the policy' (abolish/eliminate - fits perfectly). 4) Test Option C: 'Do without the policy' (manage without it - possible but 'decided to do without' suggests voluntary choice, not response to protests). 5) Test Option D: 'Do over the policy' (repeat it - illogical). Option B is the precise fit.
questions.topic: Fill in the Blanks - Phrasal Verbs

questions.text: Choose the option that best replaces the underlined segment to make the sentence grammatically correct. If the management **would have considered** the employees' proposals, the strike could have been averted.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Third Conditional structure is 'If + Past Perfect (had + V3), ... would/could/might + have + V3'. Eliminate any option in the 'If-clause' that uses 'would have' or simple past. Full Solution: The sentence describes a hypothetical past situation (Type 3 Conditional). The 'If-clause' requires Past Perfect tense ('had considered'). The original 'would have considered' is incorrect in the 'If-clause'. Option A ('had considered') fits the rule perfectly. Option B ('has considered') is Present Perfect, and Option C ('considered') is Simple Past — both wrong for Type 3 conditionals.

questions.text: 'A @ B' means 'A is the father of B'. 'A $ B' means 'A is the wife of B'. 'A # B' means 'A is the brother of B'. In the expression 'P @ Q $ R # S', how is P related to S?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode left to right. P @ Q => P father of Q. Q $ R => Q wife of R (R is husband). So P is father-in-law of R. R # S => R brother of S. Thus P is father-in-law of S. Full: Build family tree. P (Male) -> Father of Q (Female). Q (Female) -> Wife of R (Male). R (Male) -> Brother of S. Since P is father of Q, and Q is wife of R, P is father-in-law of R. Since R and S are siblings, P is father-in-law of S as well.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no improvement is required, select 'No improvement'. Having finished the assignment, the television was turned on by Rahul.

options.label: B
options.text: the television was turned on by him

options.label: C
options.text: turning on the television was done by Rahul

questions.solution: Shortcut: Dangling Modifier check. The introductory participle phrase ('Having finished...') must logically modify the subject of the main clause. A television cannot 'finish an assignment'. Step-by-step: 1) Identify the modifier: 'Having finished the assignment' implies a human doer. 2) Check main clause subject: 'the television' (inanimate, cannot finish assignment). 3) Error: Dangling modifier. 4) Evaluate options: Option A changes subject to 'Rahul' (the doer), active voice, correct. Option B retains passive voice with 'television' as subject (dangling remains). Option C retains 'turning on...' as subject (dangling remains). Option D incorrect as error exists. Option A is correct.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 12 days. A alone can do it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.solution: Shortcut (LCM method): Total work = LCM(12,20)=60 units. A+B = 60/12 =5 units/day. A = 60/20 =3 units/day. Hence B = 2 units/day → time = 60/2 =30 days. Stepwise: 1/12 - 1/20 = (5-3)/60 = 2/60 = 1/30 → 30 days.

questions.text: The length of a rectangle is 20% more than its breadth. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 132 cm, what is the area of the rectangle (in cm²)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Length : Breadth = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5. Let sides be 6x and 5x. Perimeter = 2(11x) = 22x = 132 ⇒ x = 6. Area = 6x × 5x = 30x² = 30 × 36 = 1080. Unit digit of area must be 0 (30 × 36), eliminating 960, 1008, 1152. Full: Let breadth = b. Length = 1.2b. 2(b + 1.2b) = 132 ⇒ 4.4b = 132 ⇒ b = 30. Length = 36. Area = 30 × 36 = 1080 cm².

questions.text: In the following question, symbols @, #, $, %, & are used with meanings: 'A @ B' means A > B; 'A # B' means A < B; 'A $ B' means A = B; 'A % B' means A ≥ B; 'A & B' means A ≤ B. Statements: P @ Q, Q # R, R $ S, S % T. Which conclusion definitely follows? I. P @ R II. Q $ S III. R & T
questions.solution: Shortcut: Translate symbols: @ => >, # => <, $ => =, % => ≥, & => ≤. From P > Q and Q < R we cannot relate P and R. R = S and S ≥ T gives R ≥ T, so R ≤ T is not definite. Q = S would require Q = R which is false. Hence none of the conclusions follow. Full: Using the given meanings, chain the inequalities: P > Q < R = S ≥ T. No definite relation for P > R, Q = S, or R ≤ T. Therefore none follows.

questions.text: Starting from point X, Rahul walks 10 m north, then turns right and walks 15 m, then turns left and walks 10 m, then turns right and walks 5 m. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Net North displacement = 10+10 = 20 m; Net East displacement = 15+5 = 20 m. Distance = √(20²+20²) = 20√2 m. Full: Track each turn: North 10, East 15, North 10, East 5. Final coordinates (20,20) relative to start. Apply Pythagoras to get 20√2 m.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. The audit committee has decided to ______ the discrepancies found in the quarterly financial statements.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Match the meaning to the preposition. 'Into' implies investigation/entry; 'After' implies care; 'Up' implies search/improvement; 'Out' implies caution. Context 'discrepancies' demands investigation. Full Solution: 'Look into' means to investigate or examine formally. 'Look after' means to take care of. 'Look up' means to search for information or improve. 'Look out' means to be careful. The context of 'discrepancies in financial statements' requires an investigation, making 'look into' the only correct choice.

questions.text: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of tea costing ₹60 per kg and ₹80 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹68 per kg?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Alligation): Mean price 68. Differences: 80-68=12, 68-60=8 → ratio cheaper:dearer = 12:8 = 3:2. Stepwise: Let quantities be x and y. (60x+80y)/(x+y)=68 → 60x+80y=68x+68y → 12y=8x → x/y=12/8=3/2.

questions.text: The average of 5 numbers is 40. If one number is excluded, the average becomes 38. What is the excluded number?
questions.solution: Sum of 5 numbers = 5*40 = 200. Sum of 4 numbers = 4*38 = 152. Excluded number = 200 - 152 = 48.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following number series: 4, 6, 14, 44, 178, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Observe the pattern of multiplying by consecutive integers starting from 1 and adding 2: ×1+2, ×2+2, ×3+2, ×4+2, ×5+2. Apply to last term: 178 × 5 + 2 = 892. Step-by-step: 4×1+2=6; 6×2+2=14; 14×3+2=44; 44×4+2=178; 178×5+2=892.

questions.text: Find the next term in the series: A2, D5, G9, J14, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Letters increase by 3 each step (A→D→G→J→M). Numbers increase by successive increments: +3, +4, +5, so next increment +6 → 14+6=20. Hence M20. Full: The letter pattern follows alphabetical order skipping two letters each time; the numeric pattern adds 3,4,5,6 respectively. Therefore the next term is M20.
